html:
The Dendi Kingdom was the last stronghold of the Songhai people on the middle Niger River, from the fall of their empire in 1591 to the French conquest in 1901.

Dendi had been the southern province of the Songhai Empire. When a Moroccan army of the Saadi Sultanate crushed the Songhai at the Battle of Tondibi in 1591, Askia Nuh and other Songhai leaders retreated downriver to Dendi and kept fighting. The kingdom survived for three centuries among its neighbours, though it was often split and weak.

Its centres lay around today's Gaya in Niger, Kamba in Nigeria and Malanville in Benin. France absorbed it into French West Africa in 1901. On the 1880 map the shape is drawn further north than these towns.
sum: The Dendi Kingdom was the last stronghold of the Songhai people on the middle Niger River, from the fall of their empire in 1591 to the French conquest in 1901.
